questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: The rate-limiting enzyme of glycogenolysis is:
questions.concept: Phosphorylase is activated by glucagon and adrenaline through cAMP-dependent phosphorylation and by AMP in muscle, coordinating glycogen breakdown with energy demand.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: Von Gierke disease (type I glycogen storage disease) is due to deficiency of:
options: Glucose-6-phosphatase, causing severe fasting hypoglycaemia and hepatomegaly
questions.concept: Without glucose-6-phosphatase the liver cannot release free glucose from either glycogenolysis or gluconeogenesis, giving hypoglycaemia, lactic acidosis, hyperuricaemia and hyperlipidaemia.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: McArdle disease results from deficiency of:
options: Muscle glycogen phosphorylase, causing exercise intolerance with cramps and myoglobinuria
questions.concept: Blood glucose is normal since the liver is unaffected, and there is no rise in lactate on ischaemic exercise testing. The second-wind phenomenon reflects a switch to fatty acid oxidation.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: Pompe disease is unique among glycogen storage diseases because it is:
options: A lysosomal storage disorder from acid maltase deficiency causing cardiomegaly
questions.concept: Infantile Pompe disease causes massive cardiomegaly, hypotonia and death within the first year without enzyme replacement therapy - the classic heart-in-a-box radiographic appearance.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: The principal function of the hexose monophosphate shunt is to produce:
questions.concept: NADPH maintains reduced glutathione protecting red cells from oxidative damage and supports fatty acid, cholesterol and steroid synthesis; ribose-5-phosphate supplies nucleotide synthesis.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: G6PD deficiency causes haemolysis because:
options: Failure to generate NADPH leaves red cells unable to counter oxidative stress
questions.concept: Precipitants include fava beans, primaquine, sulphonamides, nitrofurantoin and infection. Heinz bodies and bite cells appear on the smear, and enzyme assay is unreliable immediately after a haemolytic episode.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: The rate-limiting and irreversible enzyme of glycolysis is:
questions.concept: The three irreversible steps - hexokinase or glucokinase, PFK-1 and pyruvate kinase - are the regulated points and are bypassed by separate enzymes in gluconeogenesis.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: Fructose intolerance results from deficiency of:
options: Aldolase B, causing hypoglycaemia and liver damage after fructose ingestion
questions.concept: Accumulated fructose-1-phosphate traps phosphate and inhibits gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis. Essential fructosuria from fructokinase deficiency is by contrast entirely benign.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: Galactosaemia is caused by deficiency of:
questions.concept: Accumulated galactose-1-phosphate is hepatotoxic causing jaundice, hepatomegaly and E. coli sepsis; galactitol accumulation causes cataract. Galactokinase deficiency causes cataract alone.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Carbohydrate chemistry, glycogen metabolism & HMP shunt
questions.stem: Lactose intolerance results from:
options: Deficiency of intestinal lactase causing osmotic diarrhoea and flatulence after milk
questions.concept: Primary adult-type hypolactasia is very common in Asian populations. The hydrogen breath test is diagnostic, as unabsorbed lactose is fermented by colonic bacteria producing hydrogen.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: The final electron acceptor in the mitochondrial electron transport chain is:
options: Molecular oxygen, reduced to water at complex IV
questions.concept: Cyanide and carbon monoxide block cytochrome c oxidase at complex IV, halting electron flow and causing cellular hypoxia despite normal arterial oxygen - histotoxic hypoxia.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: The chemiosmotic theory states that ATP synthesis is driven by:
options: A proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane
questions.concept: Protons pumped at complexes I, III and IV return through ATP synthase. Uncouplers such as 2,4-dinitrophenol and thermogenin dissipate this gradient, releasing energy as heat rather than ATP.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: Brown adipose tissue generates heat in the newborn through:
options: Uncoupling protein 1 (thermogenin) dissipating the proton gradient
questions.concept: Non-shivering thermogenesis is essential in neonates who cannot shiver effectively. Brown fat is located interscapularly, around the neck and along the great vessels.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: Complete oxidation of one molecule of glucose yields approximately:
questions.concept: Anaerobic glycolysis alone yields only 2 ATP, which is why tissues dependent on it, such as red cells and exercising muscle in oxygen debt, generate lactate and fatigue rapidly.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: Rotenone and amytal inhibit the electron transport chain at:
questions.concept: Antimycin A blocks complex III, cyanide, carbon monoxide and azide block complex IV, and oligomycin inhibits ATP synthase itself. Malonate competitively inhibits complex II.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: Reactive oxygen species are neutralised by all EXCEPT:
questions.concept: Xanthine oxidase in fact generates superoxide, particularly during ischaemia-reperfusion. SOD converts superoxide to hydrogen peroxide, which catalase and glutathione peroxidase then detoxify.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: Selenium is an essential component of:
questions.concept: Copper and zinc are cofactors of cytosolic SOD and manganese of mitochondrial SOD, while catalase contains haem iron. Selenium deficiency causes Keshan cardiomyopathy.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: Ischaemia-reperfusion injury is mediated principally by:
options: A burst of reactive oxygen species on restoration of oxygen supply
questions.concept: During ischaemia xanthine dehydrogenase converts to xanthine oxidase and hypoxanthine accumulates; reintroducing oxygen produces a superoxide burst. This underlies myocardial stunning after reperfusion.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: Vitamin E functions principally as:
options: A lipid-soluble chain-breaking antioxidant protecting membrane polyunsaturated fatty acids
questions.concept: Vitamin C regenerates oxidised vitamin E, so the two act synergistically. Deficiency causes haemolysis and neurological damage, particularly in fat malabsorption and abetalipoproteinaemia.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.topic: Oxidative phosphorylation, ETC & free radicals
questions.stem: Mitochondrial DNA is significant clinically because it:
options: Is maternally inherited and encodes electron transport chain components
questions.concept: Heteroplasmy explains the variable severity of mitochondrial diseases such as MELAS, MERRF and Leber optic neuropathy, which affect high-energy tissues - brain, muscle, heart and retina.
